subject.title: [Analysis] Identify performance bottlenecks in native OpenClaw setup on constrained VPS

question: What scope should OpenClaw accept for the native-Linux VPS performance investigation requested by issue #53600?
rationale: The issue is valid but broad, and automation cannot safely choose the measurement environment, sufficient evidence threshold, or whether to prioritize docs-only synthesis versus new instrumentation spans.

options.title: Scope a runbook first
options.body: Publish a constrained-VPS tracing runbook from existing telemetry, then file narrow follow-ups for measured missing spans or hot paths.

options.title: Add missing spans first
options.body: Pause the broad analysis until maintainers choose specific instrumentation gaps to implement in agents, memory, Telegram, or gateway surfaces.

options.title: Defer as support-only
options.body: Close or downgrade the item if maintainers decide one-off VPS performance attribution is outside core backlog scope.

recommendation.title: Scope a runbook first
recommendation.body: Publish a constrained-VPS tracing runbook from existing telemetry, then file narrow follow-ups for measured missing spans or hot paths.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent diagnostics, OTEL, token/context, and VPS-doc history make vincentkoc the best available routing owner for scoping this investigation.
